---
title: "Events & timeline"
subtitle: "Triggers the facilitator throws into the meeting"
---

::: {.hint}
**For the facilitator.** These cards steer the dynamics of the role-play. You throw
them in **one after another** during the running meeting – verbally, as a printed card
handed to a role, or via chat/note. Each event deliberately stresses a different
**competency of lateral leadership**. You don't have to play all events: **E1–E4 are
the core**, E5–E7 are reserves for fast or large groups.
:::

## Recommended timeline (30-minute round) {#recommended-timeline}

::: {.hint}
Give the groups **enough time** – negotiation needs room to breathe. The time markers
below are meant for a 30-minute round and can easily be stretched; only throw in a new
event once the previous one has been *worked on* (see pacing notes below).
:::

::: {.timeline}

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 0–7 · Opening</span><br>
Robin (RSE) opens, presents the goal & framework, begins gathering requirements.
*No event yet.*
:::

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 7 · Event E1 — Data protection</span><br>
First stress test as soon as the meeting is running.
:::

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 13 · Event E2 — Conference deadline</span><br>
Pressure from above while Robin is still sorting things out.
:::

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 18 · Event E3 — Doctorate emergency</span><br>
A competing priority from within the team.
:::

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 23 · Event E4 — Resource loss</span><br>
The plan has to be adjusted.
:::

::: {.t-item}
<span class="t-time">Min 27–30 · Landing</span><br>
Facilitator announces “3 minutes left” → the group secures its results.
*Only sprinkle in E5–E7 if there is time/energy.*
:::

:::

## The event cards

::: {.cards}

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E1 · Core</span>
### Data protection sounds the alarm
The data protection officer gets in touch: the **video recordings of minors**
are not stored in a legally compliant way as things stand. **New consents** and an
**anonymisation pipeline** are needed before work on the video data may continue.

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** facilitator (call) or role 5 (partner school).<br>
**Stresses:** communication · conflict resolution · planning under constraints<br>
**Expected conflict:** unplanned scope vs. “but that was already settled”.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E2 · Core</span>
### The conference deadline
Petra (PI) announces enthusiastically: the project should be presented at the
specialist conference in **8 weeks**. The **abstract (4 pages) is due in 2 weeks** – with
*first results*. “I'm sure we can manage that – and tell me what you need for it!”

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** role 2 (Petra / PI).<br>
**Stresses:** leading upwards · the power of language (convincing, not pressuring) · self-leadership<br>
**Expected conflict:** “first results” vs. “data model first”.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E3 · Core</span>
### Doctorate in trouble
Mara needs a special data export **this week** for a dissertation chapter – otherwise
she misses a submission deadline of her own. “Just the table, quickly, it's really no
big deal.”

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** role 3 (Mara / domain).<br>
**Stresses:** mindful leading of others · prioritisation · expectation management<br>
**Expected conflict:** urgent individual request vs. a sustainable platform.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E4 · Core</span>
### Resource loss
Two pieces of bad news: the requested **student-assistant funding has been cut**, and
Tobi is largely unavailable for two weeks during the **exam period**. A planned task
slips.

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** facilitator + role 4 (Tobi / student assistant).<br>
**Stresses:** structuring the work · expectation management · conflict resolution<br>
**Expected conflict:** commitments from min 0–15 suddenly become unrealistic.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E5 · Reserve</span>
### The partner school wavers
Sabine makes it clear: without a **simple dashboard** that shows the school the learning
progress of *its own* classes, the school management is considering **pulling out of the
study**. Without this school, important data is missing.

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** role 5 (Sabine / partner school).<br>
**Stresses:** stakeholder communication · negotiating without power · scope<br>
**Expected conflict:** external benefit vs. research roadmap.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E6 · Reserve</span>
### Buy instead of build?
A reviewer has noted that one should check whether a **commercial tool** might be
cheaper than building it in-house. Petra would like **a short market analysis by next
week** – curious, not pushy: “Maybe we don't need to build all of this ourselves – what
do you think, Robin?”

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** role 2 (Petra / PI).<br>
**Stresses:** the power of expert knowledge · arguing on the merits · self-efficacy<br>
**Expected conflict:** the very justification for the whole undertaking is on the table.
</div>
:::

::: {.card .event}
<span class="badge">E7 · Reserve</span>
### “Just find the interesting patterns”
Mara wishes: “The platform should automatically show us the **interesting patterns**
in the learning trajectories.” When asked about criteria: “You just recognise them.”

<div class="meta">
**Who introduces it:** role 3 (Mara / domain).<br>
**Stresses:** requirements gathering · the limits of what is technically feasible · questioning technique<br>
**Expected conflict:** a vague expectation vs. a decidable specification.
</div>
:::

:::

## Pacing notes

* **Don't overload.** Only throw in an event once the previous one has been *worked on*
  (not necessarily *solved*). The goal is friction, not overwhelm.
* **Dock onto roles.** An event works most strongly when the facilitator passes it *to
  the fitting role* and that role presents it out of its own interest.
* **With strong groups** combine E5–E7 (e.g. E6 right after a self-assured plan – this
  tests the RSE's self-efficacy).
* **With groups that have stalled**, leave out an event and instead pose an *open
  question* to the RSE via a role (“What exactly do you expect from me, and by when?”).
